The longest of all discourses, this extended narrative tells of the events surrounding the Buddha ’s death. Full of vivid and moving details, it is an ideal entry point into knowing the Buddha  as a person, and understanding how the buddhist community coped with his passing
This wide-ranging sutta, the longest one in the pali canon, describes the events leading up to, during, and immediately following the death and final release (parinibbana) of the Buddha . This colorful narrative contains a wealth of Dhamma teachings, including the Buddha 's final instructions that defined how buddhism would be lived and practiced long after the Buddha 's death — even to this day. But this sutta also depicts, in simple language, the poignant human drama that unfolds among the Buddha 's many devoted followers around the time of the death of their beloved teacher.

This discourse explores the role of miracles and conversations with heavenly beings as a possible basis for faith and belief. The Buddha  does not deny the reality of such experiences, but he points out that — of all possible miracles — the only reliable one is the miracle of instruction in the proper training of the mind. As for heavenly beings, they are subject to greed, anger, and delusion, and so the information they give — especially with regard to the miracle of instruction — is not necessarily trustworthy. Thus the only valid basis for faith is the instruction that, when followed, brings about the end of one's own mental defilements.

column15: Good is restraint in the body; good is restraint in speech; good is restraint in thought. Restraint everywhere is good. The monk restrained in every way is freed from all suffering
column16: That monk who has control over his tongue, is moderate in speech, unassuming and who explains the Teaching in both letter and spirit — whatever he says is pleasing.

column14:
Sitting silent, dustless,
absorbed in jhana,
his task done, effluents gone,
ultimate goal attained:
he's what I call
a brahman.
column15:
He's called a brahman
for having banished his evil,
a contemplative
for living in consonance,
one gone forth
for having forsaken
his own impurities.
column16:
They understand for themselves 
the end of suffering in this life; 
with burden put down, detached: 
that’s who I call a brahmin

column14:
For the mind that is difficult 
to subdue, flighty, and flitting 
where’er it will, restraint is good, 
a restrained mind brings happiness.
column15:
For the one with unsettled mind, 
who does not know the True Dhamma,
whose confidence is wavering, 
wisdom is surely unfulfilled.
column16:
Knowing this body is frail like a jar,
establishing the mind like a fortress,
fight Māra with the weapon of wisdom,
guard your success, and do not be attached.

column14:
Knowing this body’s like foam, 
realizing it’s all just a mirage, 
and cutting off Māra’s blossoming, 
vanish from the King of Death
column15:
Just like a glorious flower 
that’s both colorful and fragrant, 
eloquent speech is fruitful 
for one who acts on it
column16:
Don’t find fault with others, 
with what they’ve done or left undone. 
You should only watch yourself, 
what you’ve done or left undone
column34: MŪLASARVĀSTIVĀDIVINAYA(GILGITIII.II.184); JA371:5.1; JA428:4.1; MN128:6.13; PDHP1-13:PDHP6; PLI-TV-KD10:3.1.15; UV14:UV14.10; T212.15:VGNS15.9; T213.14:VGNS14.10; UV-KG14:VUV292; UVS14:UVS14.10

column14:
If while wandering you find no partner 
equal or better than yourself, 
then firmly resolve to wander alone—
there’s no fellowship with fools
column15:
The fool who thinks they’re a fool 
is wise at least to that extent. 
But the true fool is said to be one 
who imagines that they are wise
column16:
The fool imagines that evil is sweet, 
so long as it has not yet ripened. 
But as soon as that evil ripens, 
they fall into suffering
column34: MŪLASARVĀSTIVĀDIVINAYA(GILGITIII.II.184); JA371:6.1; JA428:5.1; MN128:6.17; PDHP239-260:PDHP253; PLI-TV-KD10:3.1.19; T210.9:VGNS9.5; T212.15:VGNS15.10; T213.14:VGNS14.9; UV14:UV14.11; UV-KG14:VUV293

column14:
Regard one who sees your faults 
as a guide to a hidden treasure. 
Stay close to one so wise and astute 
who corrects you when you need it.
column16:
Good people give up everything, 
they don’t cajole for the things they desire. 
Though touched by sadness or happiness, 
the astute appear neither depressed nor elated
column17:
lake deep 
clear and unclouded, 
like clear are the astute 
when they hear the teachings.
Good people give up everything
column34: MŪLASARVĀSTIVĀDIVINAYA(GILGITIII.II.183); JA428:6.1; MN128:6.21; PDHP239-260:PDHP254; PLI-TV-KD10:3.1.23; T210.9:VGNS9.6; T213.14:VGNS14.7; THAG4.3:VNS275; THAG8.1:VNS498; UV14:UV14.8; UV-KG14:VUV290

column14:
At journey’s end, rid of sorrow; 
everywhere free, 
all ties given up, 
no fever is found in them.
column16:
Whether in village or wilderness, 
in a valley or the uplands, 
wherever the perfected ones live 
is a delightful place

column14:
Better than a thousand 
meaningless sayings 
is a single meaningful saying, 
hearing which brings you peace
column15:
The supreme conqueror is 
not he who conquers a million men in battle, 
but he who conquers a single man:  himself
column16:
Better to live a single day 
ethical and absorbed in meditation 
than to live a hundred years 
unethical and lacking immersion.

column15:
If you do something bad, 
don’t do it again and again, 
don’t set your heart on it, 
for piling up evil is suffering
column16:
Think not lightly of evil, 
that it won’t come back to you. 
The pot is filled with water 
falling drop by drop; 
the fool is filled with wickedness 
piled up bit by bit.

The Buddha  refuses to perform miracles, explaining that this is not the right way to inspire faith. He goes on to tell the story of a monk whose misguided quest for answers led him as far as Brahmā
This discourse explores the role of miracles and conversations with heavenly beings as a possible basis for faith and belief. The Buddha  does not deny the reality of such experiences, but he points out that — of all possible miracles — the only reliable one is the miracle of instruction in the proper training of the mind. As for heavenly beings, they are subject to greed, anger, and delusion, and so the information they give — especially with regard to the miracle of instruction — is not necessarily trustworthy. Thus the only valid basis for faith is the instruction that, when followed, brings about the end of one's own mental defilements.

The longest of all discourses, this extended narrative tells of the events surrounding the Buddha ’s death. Full of vivid and moving details, it is an ideal entry point into knowing the Buddha  as a person, and understanding how the buddhist community coped with his passing
This wide-ranging sutta, the longest one in the pali canon, describes the events leading up to, during, and immediately following the death and final release (parinibbana) of the Buddha . This colorful narrative contains a wealth of Dhamma teachings, including the Buddha 's final instructions that defined how buddhism would be lived and practiced long after the Buddha 's death — even to this day. But this sutta also depicts, in simple language, the poignant human drama that unfolds among the Buddha 's many devoted followers around the time of the death of their beloved teacher.

After hearing a love song from a god of music, the Buddha  engages in a deep discussion with sakka on the conditioned origin of attachment and suffering
Sakka, the deva-king, asks the Buddha about the sources of conflict, and about the path of practice that can bring it to an end. This discourse ends with a humorous account about Sakka's frustration in trying to learn the Dhamma from other contemplatives. It's hard to find a teacher when you're a king.

The dart of doubt and uncertainty has lain within me for a long time, but the Buddha  has plucked it out
column16:

The Buddha  refutes a jain theory of kamma, which claims that one's present experience is determined solely by one's actions in past lives, and that the effects of past unskillful actions can be "burned away" through austerity practices. It is precisely this interaction of present and past that opens up the very possibility of awakening

column3: Longer Discourse on the Full-Moon Night
column14:
On a lovely full moon night, one of the mendicants presents the Buddha  with a series of questions that go to the heart of the teaching. But when he hears of the doctrine of not-self, another mendicant is unable to grasp the meaning
A thorough discussion of issues related to the five aggregates. Toward the end of the discussion, a monk thinks that he has found a loophole in the teaching. The way the Buddha  handles this incident shows the proper use of the teachings on the aggregates: not as a metaphysical theory, but as a tool for questioning clinging and so gaining release
column15:
Five grasping aggregates are rooted in desire, the desire and greed for them is the grasping,
An uneducated ordinary person has not seen the noble ones regard form, feelings,perceptions, fabrications or consciousness  as self, self as having them, form … in self, or self in form ...
The pleasure and happiness that arise from form: this is its gratification. That Form is impermanent, suffering, and perishable: this is its drawback.Removing And giving up desire and greed for form: this is its escape.
column16:
Four primary elements are the reason why the aggregate of form is found. Contact Is the reason why the aggregates of feeling … perception … and choices are found. Name And form are the reasons why the aggregate of consciousness is found
So you should truly see any kind  of form, feeling, perceptions, fabrications and consciousness  at all—past, future, or present; internal or external; coarse or fine; inferior or superior; far or near, with right understanding: ‘this is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self.
Seeing this, a learned noble disciple grows disillusioned with form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness.
Being disillusioned, desire fades away. When desire fades away they’re freed. When they’re freed, they know they’re freed

column14:
Surrounded by many well-practiced mendicants, the Buddha  teaches mindfulness of breathing in detail, showing how they relate to the four kinds of mindfulness meditation
One of the most important texts for beginning and veteran meditators alike, this sutta is the Buddha 's roadmap to the entire course of meditation practice, using the vehicle of breath meditation. The simple practice of mindfulness of breathing leads the practitioner gradually through 16 successive phases of development, culminating in full awakening
column15:
An assembly such as this is worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, worthy of hospitality, worthy of a religious donation, worthy of greeting with joined palms, and is the supreme field of merit for the world
Whenever a mendicant knows that they breathe heavily, or lightly, or experiencing the whole body, or stilling the body’s motion—at that time they’re meditating by observing an aspect of the body. For I say that the in-breaths and out-breaths are an aspect of the body
Whenever a mendicant practices breathing while experiencing the mind, or gladdening the mind, or immersing the mind in samādhi, or freeing the mind—at that time they meditate observing an aspect of the mind, there is no development of mindfulness of breathing for someone who is unmindful and lacks awareness, I say
On whatever occasion the monk remains focused on the body, feelings, mind and dhammas. putting aside greed & distress with reference to the world, on that occasion his mindfulness is steady & without lapse then mindfulness as a factor for awakening becomes aroused. they develop it and perfect it.
column16:
In this saṅgha there are perfected mendicants, who have ended the defilements, with  the ending of the five lower fetters, with the ending of three fetters, and the weakening of greed, hate, and delusion, are once-returners, with the ending of three fetters are stream-enterers, who  are committed to developing the four kinds of mindfulness meditation … the four right efforts … the four bases of psychic power … the five faculties … the five powers … the seven awakening factors … the noble eightfold path, to developing the meditation on love …compassion … rejoicing … equanimity … ugliness …impermanence, to developing the meditation on mindfulness of breathing
Whenever a mendicant practices breathing while experiencing rapture, or experiencing bliss, or experiencing these emotions, or stilling these emotions—at that time they meditate observing an aspect of feelings, keen, aware, and mindful, rid of desire and aversion for the world. For I say that close attention to the in-breaths and out-breaths is an aspect of feelings
Whenever a mendicant practices breathing while observing impermanence, or observing fading away,or observing cessation, or observing letting go—at that time they meditate observing an aspect of principles—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of desire and aversion for the world. Having Seen with wisdom the giving up of desire and aversion, they watch over closely with equanimity
As they live mindfully in this way they investigate, explore, and inquire into that principle with wisdom has activated the awakening factor of investigation of principles, in this way their energy is roused up and unflagging, activated the awakening factor of energy. When they’re energetic, spiritual rapture arises. When the mind is full of rapture, the body and mind become tranquil, when the body is tranquil and they feel bliss, the mind becomes immersed in samādhi.They Closely watch over that mind immersed in samādhi. which rely on seclusion, fading away, and cessation, and ripen as letting go

Whenever a mendicant knows that they breathe heavily, or lightly, or experiencing the whole body, or stilling the body’s motion—at that time they’re meditating by observing an aspect of the body. For I say that the in-breaths and out-breaths are an aspect of the body
Whenever a mendicant practices breathing while experiencing the mind, or gladdening the mind, or immersing the mind in samādhi, or freeing the mind—at that time they meditate observing an aspect of the mind, there is no development of mindfulness of breathing for someone who is unmindful and lacks awareness, I say
On whatever occasion the monk remains focused on the body, feelings, mind and dhammas. putting aside greed & distress with reference to the world, on that occasion his mindfulness is steady & without lapse then mindfulness as a factor for awakening becomes aroused. they develop it and perfect it.
column16:
In this saṅgha there are perfected mendicants, who have ended the defilements, with  the ending of the five lower fetters, with the ending of three fetters, and the weakening of greed, hate, and delusion, are once-returners, with the ending of three fetters are stream-enterers, who  are committed to developing the four kinds of mindfulness meditation … the four right efforts … the four bases of psychic power … the five faculties … the five powers … the seven awakening factors … the noble eightfold path, to developing the meditation on love …compassion … rejoicing … equanimity … ugliness …impermanence, to developing the meditation on mindfulness of breathing
Whenever a mendicant practices breathing while experiencing rapture, or experiencing bliss, or experiencing these emotions, or stilling these emotions—at that time they meditate observing an aspect of feelings, keen, aware, and mindful, rid of desire and aversion for the world. For I say that close attention to the in-breaths and out-breaths is an aspect of feelings
Whenever a mendicant practices breathing while observing impermanence, or observing fading away,or observing cessation, or observing letting go—at that time they meditate observing an aspect of principles—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of desire and aversion for the world. Having Seen with wisdom the giving up of desire and aversion, they watch over closely with equanimity
As they live mindfully in this way they investigate, explore, and inquire into that principle with wisdom has activated the awakening factor of investigation of principles, in this way their energy is roused up and unflagging, activated the awakening factor of energy. When they’re energetic, spiritual rapture arises. When the mind is full of rapture, the body and mind become tranquil, when the body is tranquil and they feel bliss, the mind becomes immersed in samādhi.They Closely watch over that mind immersed in samādhi. which rely on seclusion, fading away, and cessation, and ripen as letting go

This focuses on the first aspect of mindfulness meditation, the observation of the body. This set of practices, simple as they seem, have far-reaching benefits.
 This sutta serves as a companion to the anapanasati sutta, and explains the importance of establishing a broad awareness of the body in meditation to develop jhana
column15:
As they meditate like this—diligent, keen, and resolute—memories and thoughts of the lay life are given up. Their Mind becomes stilled internally; it settles, unifies, and becomes immersed in samādhi.That’s How a mendicant develops mindfulness of the body
Anyone who has developed and cultivated mindfulness of the body includes all of the skillful qualities that play a part in realization, and Māra cannot find a vulnerability and doesn’t get hold of them
column16:
1 mindfulness of breathing 2 whatever posture their body is in, they know it, 3  mindful and alert in every activity 4 examines their own body full of many kinds of filth, 5 in this body there is the earth, water, fire and air,  elements 6 compare  corpses with their own body:‘this body is also of that same nature, 7 first jhana, 8 second jhana, 9 third jhana, 10 fourth jhana with similes
Benefits: they prevail over desire and discontent, over fear and dread, endure cold, heat, hunger, and thirst and disagreeable things,  get the four absorption, wield the many kinds of psychic power, understand the minds of other beings, recollect many kinds of past lives, with clairvoyant see sentient beings passing away and being reborn, they realize the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom in this very life

column3: Longer Discourse on the Lion’s Roar
column14:
The Buddha  expounds the ten powers of a tathagata, his four kinds of intrepidity, and other superior qualities which entitle him to "roar his lion's roar in the assemblies.
Disrobed monk, sunakkhata, attacks the Buddha ’s teaching because it merely leads to the end of suffering. The Buddha  counters that this is, in fact, praise, and goes on to enumerate his many profound and powerful achievements.
column15:
With these the Buddha  claims the bull’s place, roars his lion’s roar in the assemblies, and turns the holy wheel
When their body breaks up, after death, is reborn in a place of loss, a bad place: hell where they experience exclusively painful feelings, animal realm where they experience painful feelings and the ghost realm where they experience many painful feelings
The Buddha  practiced a spiritual path consisting of four factors.
column16:
Blessed one wields the many kinds of psychic powers, the ten powers of a realized one,  has four kinds of self-assurance where the realized one approaches the eight assemblies, sees the four kinds of reproduction, he understands the 5 destinations and  the path and practice that leads to each one
 when their body breaks up, after death, is reborn in a good place: human beings where  they experience many pleasant feelings, a heavenly realm where they experience exclusively pleasant feelings or nibbana the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom in this very life
Ultimate self-mortifier,  the ultimate rough-liver, the ultimate one living in disgust at sin, in ultimate seclusion
column17: Hell like pit of coals, animal realm like a sewer full with feces, ghost realm like tree growing on rugged ground, human beings like  a tree growing on smooth ground, heaven realms like a stilt longhouse, nibbana like a lotus pond with clear, sweet, cool water
column30: DIVY27; SF141; SF142; SF243; SF244; SF261; SF262; SF60; SF91; SF95; SF96; SHT-SUTTA28; SHT-SUTTA36

column14: The Buddha  explains how one can make a wish to be reborn in different realms
column15: Take a mendicant who has faith, ethics, learning, generosity, and wisdom.
column16: They can choose any realm they want or liberation in this life. They settle on that thought, stabilize it and develop it. Those Choices and meditations of theirs, developed and cultivated like this, lead to rebirth there

column14: The Buddha  describes his own practice of the meditation on emptiness. The Buddha  instructs ven. Ananda on the practice that leads to the "entry into emptiness," the doorway to liberation
column15: Not attending to the perception of human being, not attending to the perception of wilderness, perception of earth, perception of the dimension of the infinitude of space, perception of the dimension of the infinitude of consciousness, perception of the dimension of nothingness, singleness based on the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception, that is not emptiness, namely that associated with the six sense fields dependent on this body and conditioned by life.
column16: Attends to the singleness based on the theme-less concentration of awareness. His mind takes pleasure, finds satisfaction, settles, & indulges in its theme,  he discerns that 'whatever is fabricated & mentally fashioned is inconstant & subject to cessation.' For him — thus knowing, thus seeing — the mind is released from the effluent of sensuality, of becoming,  of ignorance

column14:
A group of mendicants have taken to socializing too much, so the Buddha  teaches on the importance of seclusion in order to enter fully into emptiness
Issues include the need for seclusion as a conducive setting for the practice, types of conversation and thinking that are beneficial and harmful for the practice, the dangers of being distracted by visitors, and the proper attitude to have toward one's teacher
The Buddha  instructs Ananda on several practical aspects of the meditative dwelling in emptiness, a mode of awareness that can ultimately bring the meditator to the threshold of awakening
column15:
I do not envision even a single form whose change & alteration would not give rise to sorrow, lamentation, pain, distress, & despair in one who is passionate for it and takes delight in it
May I enter & remain in internal emptiness,' then he should get the mind steadied right within, settled, unified, & concentrated
He discerns, 'while I am attending to the imperturbable, my mind takes pleasure, finds satisfaction, grows steady, & indulges in the imperturbable.' In this way he is alert there.
Mind inclines to walking, to standing... to sitting... to lying down, he lies down, talking  [thinking,] 'while doing thus, no desire and aversion, no evil, unskillful qualities will take possession of me.' In this way he is alert there
I will engage in speech about self-effacement that helps open the heart and leads solely to disillusionment, dispassion, cessation, peace, insight, awakening, and extinguishment. That is, talk about fewness of wishes, contentment, seclusion, aloofness, arousing energy, ethics, immersion, wisdom, freedom, and the knowledge and vision of freedom
As he stays keeping track of arising & passing away with regard to these five clinging-aggregates, he abandons any conceit that 'I am' with regard to these five clinging-aggregates
While meditating withdrawn, they’re visited by a stream of brahmins and householders of the city and country. When This happens, they enjoy infatuation, fall into greed, and return to indulgence. They’re Ruined by bad, unskillful qualities that are corrupted, leading to future lives, hurtful, resulting in suffering and future rebirth, old age, and death.
column16:
A monk who lives alone, withdrawn from the group, can expect to enter & remain in the awareness-release that is temporary and pleasing, or in the awareness-release that is not-temporary and beyond provocation, the pleasure of self-awakening
Quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unskillful qualities, enters and remains in the first absorption … second absorption … third absorption … fourth absorption
They understand: ‘I am focusing on emptiness internally, externally or both but my mind isn’t eager, confident, settled, and decided, in this way he is clearly aware and he should get the mind steadied right within, settled, unified, & concentrated in his first theme of concentration
But I will think the kind of thought that is noble and emancipating, and brings one who practices it to the complete ending of suffering. That is, thoughts of renunciation, good will, and harmlessness.’ In This way they are aware of the situation.
Not in speech that is low, crude, ordinary, ignoble, and pointless: talk about kings, bandits, and ministers; talk about armies, threats, and wars; talk about food, drink, clothes, and beds; talk about garlands and fragrances; talk about family, vehicles, villages, towns, cities, and countries; talk about women and heroes; street talk and well talk; talk about the departed; motley talk; tales of land and sea; and talk about being reborn in this or that state of existence
Meditate observing rise and fall in these five grasping aggregates: ‘such is form, such is the origin of form, such is the ending of form. Such Is feeling … such is perception … such are choices …such is consciousness, such is the origin of consciousness, such is the ending of consciousness
When the teacher teaches the Dhamma out of kindness and compassion: ‘this is for your welfare. This is for your happiness.’ But Their disciples don’t want to listen. They don’t pay attention or apply their minds to understand

Issues include the need for seclusion as a conducive setting for the practice, types of conversation and thinking that are beneficial and harmful for the practice, the dangers of being distracted by visitors, and the proper attitude to have toward one's teacher

column15:
I do not envision even a single form whose change & alteration would not give rise to sorrow, lamentation, pain, distress, & despair in one who is passionate for it and takes delight in it
May I enter & remain in internal emptiness,' then he should get the mind steadied right within, settled, unified, & concentrated
He discerns, 'while I am attending to the imperturbable, my mind takes pleasure, finds satisfaction, grows steady, & indulges in the imperturbable.' In this way he is alert there.
Mind inclines to walking, to standing... to sitting... to lying down, he lies down, talking  [thinking,] 'while doing thus, no desire and aversion, no evil, unskillful qualities will take possession of me.' In this way he is alert there
I will engage in speech about self-effacement that helps open the heart and leads solely to disillusionment, dispassion, cessation, peace, insight, awakening, and extinguishment. That is, talk about fewness of wishes, contentment, seclusion, aloofness, arousing energy, ethics, immersion, wisdom, freedom, and the knowledge and vision of freedom
As he stays keeping track of arising & passing away with regard to these five clinging-aggregates, he abandons any conceit that 'I am' with regard to these five clinging-aggregates
While meditating withdrawn, they’re visited by a stream of brahmins and householders of the city and country. When This happens, they enjoy infatuation, fall into greed, and return to indulgence. They’re Ruined by bad, unskillful qualities that are corrupted, leading to future lives, hurtful, resulting in suffering and future rebirth, old age, and death.
column16:
A monk who lives alone, withdrawn from the group, can expect to enter & remain in the awareness-release that is temporary and pleasing, or in the awareness-release that is not-temporary and beyond provocation, the pleasure of self-awakening
Quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unskillful qualities, enters and remains in the first absorption … second absorption … third absorption … fourth absorption
They understand: ‘I am focusing on emptiness internally, externally or both but my mind isn’t eager, confident, settled, and decided, in this way he is clearly aware and he should get the mind steadied right within, settled, unified, & concentrated in his first theme of concentration
But I will think the kind of thought that is noble and emancipating, and brings one who practices it to the complete ending of suffering. That is, thoughts of renunciation, good will, and harmlessness.’ In This way they are aware of the situation.
Not in speech that is low, crude, ordinary, ignoble, and pointless: talk about kings, bandits, and ministers; talk about armies, threats, and wars; talk about food, drink, clothes, and beds; talk about garlands and fragrances; talk about family, vehicles, villages, towns, cities, and countries; talk about women and heroes; street talk and well talk; talk about the departed; motley talk; tales of land and sea; and talk about being reborn in this or that state of existence
Meditate observing rise and fall in these five grasping aggregates: ‘such is form, such is the origin of form, such is the ending of form. Such Is feeling … such is perception … such are choices …such is consciousness, such is the origin of consciousness, such is the ending of consciousness
When the teacher teaches the Dhamma out of kindness and compassion: ‘this is for your welfare. This is for your happiness.’ But Their disciples don’t want to listen. They don’t pay attention or apply their minds to understand

column14: Venerable Ananda is invited by the Buddha  to speak on the Buddha ’s amazing qualities, and proceeds to list a series of apparently miraculous events accompanying his birth. The Buddha  caps it off by explaining what he thinks is really amazing about himself
column15: The realized one knows feelings as they arise, as they remain, and as they go away. He Knows perceptions as they arise, as they remain, and as they go away. He Knows thoughts as they arise, as they remain, and as they go away
column16: When the being intent on awakening passes away from the host of joyful gods, he is conceived in his mother’s womb, a magnificent light appears, surpassing the glory of the gods, ‘as soon as he’s born, the being intent on awakening stands firm with his own feet on the ground and makes this dramatic statement: “I am the foremost in the world! I am the eldest in the world! I am the best in the world! This is my last rebirth. Now there are no more future lives

column14: Venerable Bakkula, regarded as the healthiest of the mendicants, explains to an old friend his strict and austere practice. The unusual form of this discourse suggests it was added to the canon some time after the Buddha ’s death
column15: In these eighty years, I don’t recall that any perceptions or thought of sensuality … ill will … or cruelty has ever arisen in me. for seven days I ate the nation’s alms-food as a debtor. Then On the eighth day I became enlightened
column16: I don’t recall accepting a robe from a householder, accepting an invitation, sitting down inside a house, getting caught up in the details of female’s appearance, teaching a female, even so much as a four line verse … going to the nuns’ quarters,  dependence … being looked after by a novice … bathing in the sauna …bathing with bath powder, being ill, being presented with medicine,  leaning on a headrest …preparing a cot, commencing the rainy season residence in the neighborhood of a village

column14: By analogy with the taming of an elephant, the Buddha  explains how he tames his disciples.
column15: If a mendicant passes away having ended the defilements—whether as a senior, middle, or junior—they’re considered as a mendicant who passed away tamed.                  This should be expanded as in mn 107
column16: Listen to the Buddha  dhamma, conviction, give away posessions, renounce sensual pleasures, pattimokka sila, guard 6 senses, give up 5 hindrances , sati sampajjano of body, felling , mind & mental contents, 4 jhannas, recollection past lives, clairvoyance, knowing 4 noble truths, gaining ultimate freedom
column17: Taming of an elephant like the gradual training

column14: Success in the spiritual life does not depend on any vows you may or may not make, but on whether you practice well
column15: Does the desire for awakening get in the way of awakening? According to this discourse, the question of desiring or not desiring is irrelevant as long as one develops the appropriate qualities that constitute the path to awakening. The discourse is also very clear on the point that there are right and wrong paths of practice
column16: The apropriate way of practice is who have right view, right thought, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion. regardless of  whether they make a wish or not, or both or they neither
column17: Right and wrong way to get oil, milk, butter  or fire, like right and wrong paths of spirituality

column14: A lay person becomes confused when encouraged to develop the “limitless” and “expansive” liberations, and asks venerable anuruddha to explain whether they are the same or different
column15:
Limitless release of the heart, it’s when a mendicant meditates spreading a heart full of love, compassion, rejoice and equanimity to one direction, and to the second, and to the third, and to the fourth. In the same way above, below, across, everywhere, all around, to the whole world—abundant, expansive, limitless, free of enmity and ill will
Gods of limited radiance, gods of limitless radiance,  gods of corrupted radiance, gods of pure radiance, when who meditates determined on pervading according after death they are reborn like that
Corrupted radiance, their physical discomfort is not completely settled, their dullness and drowsiness is not completely eradicated, and their restlessness and remorse is not completely eliminated. Because Of this they practice absorption dimly, as it were
column16:
Expansive  release of the heart it’s when a mendicant meditates determined on pervading the extent of a single tree root, 2 or 3 trees roots a single village district … two or three village districts … a single kingdom … two or three kingdoms … this land surrounded by ocean as expansive with his kasina sign
It’s not that those deities think, ‘what we have is permanent, lasting, and eternal.’ Rather, wherever those deities cling, that’s where they take pleasure
Pure radiance’. Their Physical discomfort is completely settled, their dullness and drowsiness is completely eradicated, and their restlessness and remorse is completely eliminated. Because Of this they don’t practice absorption dimly, as it were
column17:
Oil lamps  with different colors of light but same radiance
oil lamp was burning with impure oil and impure wick like jhanas not completely  mastered

column14: A second discourse set at the quarrel of kosambi, this depicts the Buddha , having failed to achieve reconciliation between the disputing mendicants, leaving the monastery. He spends time in the wilderness before encountering an inspiring community of practicing monks. There he discusses in detail obstacles to meditation that he encountered before awakening
column15:
He abused me, he hit me! 
He beat me, he took from me!’ 
Those who cling to hate like this 
Never settle their enmity. .Those Who never cling to hate 
Always settle their enmity
If you find an alert companion, 
A wise and virtuous friend, 
Then, overcoming all challenges, 
Wander with them, joyful and mindful     living in harmony, appreciating each other, without quarreling, blending like milk and water, and regarding each other with kindly eyes
When I understood that doubt, loss of focus, dullness and drowsiness, terror, excitement, discomfort,excessive energy, overly lax energy, longing,perception of diversity, and excessive concentration on forms are corruptions of the mind, I gave them up
column16:
For enmity in this world 
Is never settled by enmity. 
It’s only settled by love: 
This is an ancient principle  it’s better to wander alone, 
For a fool can never be a friend. 
Wander alone and do no wrong, 
At ease like a tusker in the wild
 consistently treat these venerables with kindness by way of body, speech, and mind, both in public and in private. I Think: ‘why don’t I set aside my own ideas and just go along with these venerables’ 
I Developed immersion while placing the mind and keeping it connected; without placing the mind, but just keeping it connected; without placing the mind or keeping it connected; with rapture; without rapture; with pleasure; with equanimity, when I had developed immersion in these ways, the knowledge and vision arose in me: ‘my freedom is unshakable

column3: Shorter Discourse on the Mass of Suffering
column14:
What mental qualities must be abandoned in order to free oneself of greed, aversion, and delusion? Can painful austerities be used to purify oneself and burn away the karmic fruit of past misdeeds? Through question-and-answer dialogues with the lay follower mahanama and with a group of jain ascetics, the Buddha  lays these questions to rest.
A lay person is puzzled at how, despite their long practice, they still have greedy or hateful thoughts. The Buddha  explains the importance of absorption meditation for letting go such attachments. But he also criticizes self-mortification, and recounts a previous dialog with jain ascetics

column15:
The fully awakened Buddha  rolled forth the supreme wheel of dhamma. It is the teaching, advocating, establishing, clarifying, analyzing, and revealing of the four noble truths.”
The noble truth of the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering:     right view: knowing about suffering, the origin of suffering, the cessation of suffering, and the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering, right thought: thoughts of renunciation, good will, and harmlessness.   right speech: refraining from lying, divisive speech, harsh speech, and talking nonsense. right action? Refraining From killing living creatures, stealing, and sexual misconduct
column16:
The noble truth of suffering: rebirth, old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress are suffering; not getting what you wish for. In brief, the five grasping aggregates are suffering.  the noble truth of the origin of suffering:  is, craving for sensual pleasures, craving to continue existence, and craving to end existence.  the  noble truth of the cessation of suffering? It’s The fading away and cessation of that very same craving with nothing left over
Right livelihood? It’s When a noble disciple earns a living by right livelihood. right effort? It’s When a mendicant generates enthusiasm, tries, makes an effort, exerts the mind, and strives so that bad, unskillful qualities don’t arise, that have arisen are given up. so that skillful qualities arise  and are completed by development. right mindfulness: observing an aspect of the body, feelings … mind … principles keen, aware, and mindful, rid of desire and aversion for the world. right samadhi are 4 jhanas

column15:
Ant-hill’ is a term for this body liable to impermanence; thinking  all night about what you did during the day—this is the fuming at night. The Work you apply yourself to during the day by body, speech, and mind after thinking about it all night—this is the flaming by day; brahmin’ is a term for the realized one;
‘sage’ is a term for the trainee mendicant; sword’ is a term for noble wisdom.
column16:
‘Digging’ is a term for being energetic; throw out the bar’ means ‘give up ignorance; throw out the bullfrog’ means ‘give up anger and distress; throw out the forked path’ means ‘give up doubt; throw out the box’ means ‘give up the five hindrances; throw out the tortoise’ means ‘give up the five grasping aggregates; throw out the axe and block’ means ‘give up the five kinds of sensual stimulation; throw out the lump of meat’ means ‘give up desire with relishing; dragon’ is a term for a mendicant who has ended the defilements. 
This is the meaning of: ‘leave the dragon!, Worship the dragon

column14:

column15:
Puṇṇa mantāṇiputta is fortunate, so very fortunate,in that his sensible spiritual companions praise him point by point in the presence of the teacher, and that the teacher seconds that appreciation.

column16:

Purification of ethics is only for the sake of purification of mind,  is only for the sake of purification of view,  is only for the sake of purification through overcoming doubt, is only for the sake of purification of knowledge and vision of the variety of paths, is only for the sake of purification of knowledge and vision of the practice, is only for the sake of purification of knowledge and vision  is only for the sake of extinguishment by not grasping.

column14:
This is one of the most important biographical discourses, telling the Buddha ’s experiences from leaving home to realizing awakening. Throughout, he was driven by the imperative to fully escape from rebirth and suffering
Most of us spend a good part of our lives looking for happiness in all the wrong places. In this sutta the Buddha  recounts the story of his own search and points out where a true and lasting happiness can be found
column15:
Ignoble search is when someone who is themselves liable to be reborn seeks what is also liable to be reborn, to grow old, fall sick, die, sorrow, and become corrupted, they seek what is also liable to these things. And noble search is understanding the drawbacks in these things, they seek the unaging, unailing, undying, sorrowless, uncorrupted supreme sanctuary, nibbana
I approached āḷāra kālāma and uddaka, son of rāma. I quickly memorized those teaching and with faith, energy, mindfulness, samadhi , and wisdom and  I quickly realized that teaching with my own insight
This principle I have discovered is deep, hard to see, hard to understand, peaceful, sublime, beyond the scope of reason, subtle, comprehensible to the astute
Sir, let the blessed one teach the dhamma! Let the holy one teach the dhamma! 
There are beings with little dust in their eyes. They’re in decline because they haven’t heard the teaching.There Will be those who understand the teaching!
Quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unskillful qualities, enters and remains in the 9 jhanas
column16:
Partners and children, male and female bondservants,  cattle, and gold and money are liable to corruption. These Attachments are liable to corruption. Someone Who is tied, infatuated, and attached to such things themselves liable to corruption
This teaching doesn’t lead to disillusionment, dispassion, cessation, peace, insight, awakening, and extinguishment
 people like attachment, they love it and enjoy it. 
It’s hard for them to see this thing; that is, specific conditionality, dependent origination, the stilling of all activities, the letting go of all attachments, the ending of craving, fading away, cessation, extinguishmen
I have achieved the deathless! I shall instruct you, I will teach you the dhamma. 
By practicing as instructed you will soon realize the supreme end of the spiritual path in this very life
Ascetics and brahmins who enjoy these five kinds of sensual stimulation tied, infatuated, attached, blind to the drawbacks, and not understanding the escape. You should understand that they have met with calamity and disaster, and are vulnerable to the wicked one

column16: Arahants ended the defilements, non-returners ending of the five lower fetters, ending of three fetters, and the weakening of greed, hate, and delusion, are once-returners, ending of three fetters are stream-enterers,  followers by faith will safely cross over to the far shore.
column17: Intelligent cowherd that drove his cattle across the river Ganges like the Buddha instruct his disciples to nibbana

column14:
Even though the Buddha  did not usually seek debates, he knew how to reply effectively when attacked. In this discourse, he gets saccaka — who uses a variety of cheap debater's tricks — to trip over those tricks. However, the Buddha  goes beyond simply defeating saccaka in debate. He then takes the opportunity to teach him the dhamma.
Saccaka was a debater, who challenged the Buddha  to a contest. Despite his bragging, the Buddha  is not at all perturbed at his attacks
column15:
Form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness are impermanent therefore they are not-self. All Conditions are impermanent. All things are not-self
That’s how to define one of my disciples who follows instructions and responds to advice; who has gone beyond doubt, got rid of indecision, gained assurance, and is independent of others in the teacher’s instructions
column16:

column14:
In a less confrontational meeting, the Buddha  and saccaka discuss the difference between physical and mental development. The Buddha  gives a long account of the various practices he did before awakening, detailing the astonishing lengths he took to mortify the body.
In response to an insinuating remark — that his ability not to be overcome by pleasure and pain is due simply to the fact that he never experienced any intense pleasures or pains — the Buddha  recounts the pains he endured in his austerities, and the pleasures that attended the path to and his attainment of awakening.
column15:
Someone whose mind is not occupied by both pleasant and painful feelings like this is developed in physical endurance and in mind
History of the steps the Buddha  took since he gone forth and set out to discover what is skillful, seeking the supreme state of sublime peace
Don't be afraid of jhanas  pleasure, for it has nothing to do with sensual pleasures or unskillful qualities
column16:
When they experience pleasant feeling they don’t become full of lust for it. Then That pleasant feeling ceases. And When it ceases, painful feeling arises. When They experience painful feelings they don’t sorrow or lament, because their physical endurance is developed, pleasant feelings don’t occupy the mind. And because their mind is developed, painful feelings don’t occupy the mind.
Approached, learn & memorize from āḷāra kālāma who thought the dimension of nothingness, approached uddaka, son of rāma who thought him the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception, tortured mind with mind, breathless absorption, cutting off food, and then turn to the 4 jhanas and 3 knowledges
Experienced painful, feelings due to overexertion,  the Buddha  did not achieved any superhuman distinction in knowledge and vision, because his body was disturbed

column3: Shorter Discourse on the Ending of Craving
column14: Moggallāna visits the heaven of sakka, the lord of gods, to see whether he really understands what the Buddha  is teaching
column15: Briefly define a bhikkhu  who is freed with the ending of craving, who has reached the ultimate end, the ultimate sanctuary, the ultimate spiritual life, the ultimate goal, and is best among gods and humans
column16: When a bhikkhu has heard that nothing is worth insisting on, they directly know all things, they completely understand all things, then  when they experience any kind of feeling—pleasant, unpleasant, or neutral—they meditate observing impermanence, dispassion, cessation, and letting go in those feelings. Meditating In this way, they don’t grasp at anything in the world. Not Grasping, they’re not anxious and they personally become extinguished

column3: Longer Discourse on the Ending of Craving
column13: Not me, Not mine, Non self
column14:
To counter the wrong view that a self-identical consciousness transmigrates from one life to the next, the Buddha  teaches dependent origination, showing that consciousness invariably arises dependent on conditions.
A long discourse in which the Buddha  discusses how to understand the role of consciousness — as a process — in the process of birth in a way that actually can lead to the end of birth
column15:
Wrong view: consciousness is he who speaks and feels and experiences the results of good and bad deeds in all the different realms, that roams and transmigrates,
When these three things come together—the mother and father come together, the mother is in the fertile part of her menstrual cycle, and the spirit being reborn is present—an embryo is conceived.
When this exists, that is; due to the arising of this, that arises. that is the 12 links chain
 a realized one arises in the world, a householder hears that teaching and gain faith after some time they give up a large or small fortune, and a large or small family circle, and go forth from the lay life to homelessness
When they perceive something from the senses if it’s pleasant they don’t desire it, and if it’s unpleasant they don’t dislike it. They live with mindfulness of the body established and a limitless heart. And They truly understand the freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom where those arisen bad, unskillful qualities cease without anything left over
Teaching that is good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, with the right meaning and phrasing
He knows that pure and bright as this view is for crossing over, not for holding on, so he doesn't treasure it, nor treat it as his own,
column16:
Right views, consciousness is reckoned according to the specific conditions dependent upon which of the 6 senses it arises
4 fuels of life: solid food, whether coarse or fine; contact is the second, mental intention the third, and consciousness the fourth, and their source is craving
When this doesn’t exist, that is not; due to the cessation of this, that ceases. that is the 12 links chain
Have this noble spectrum of ethics, this noble sense restraint, and this noble mindfulness and situational awareness, then  give up these five hindrances that weaken wisdom. 
Then, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unskillful qualities, they enter and remain in the 4 jhanas
Having given up favoring and opposing, when they experience any kind of feeling—pleasant, unpleasant, or neutral—they don’t approve, welcome, or keep clinging to it. As A result, relishing of feelings ceases. When Their relishing ceases, grasping ceases. When grasping ceases, continued existence ceases. When continued existence ceases, rebirth ceases. When rebirth ceases, old age and death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress cease. That Is how this entire mass of suffering cease
This teaching is visible in this very life, immediately effective, inviting inspection, relevant, so that sensible people can know it for themselves,
Free of doubt about dependent origination, when truly sees with right understanding that this has come to be,  this has originated with that as fuel, that when that fuel ceases, what has come to be is liable to cease. free of doubt of present, past and future of ‘am I exist ? Am I not exist? What am I? How am I? This sentient being—where did it come from? And where will it go?,Don't acknowledge another teacher, don't believe that the observances and, superstitious rites are important things

The Buddha  outlines the full course of training by which a meditator may earn the right to call him- or herself a true contemplative.
column15:
I declare to you: you who seek the recluse’s status, do not fall short of the goal of recluseship while there is more to be done.
Should train like this: ‘we will undertake and follow the things that make one an ascetic and a brahmin. That way our label will be accurate and our claim correct
column16:

What would it take to live in solitude in the wilderness, completely free of fear? The Buddha  explains
The Buddha  explains the difficulties of living in the wilderness, and how they are overcome by purity of conduct and meditation. He recounts some of the fears and obstacles he faced during his own practice
column15:
Remote lodgings in the wilderness and the forest are challenging. It’s hard to maintain seclusion and hard to find joy in it. Staying Alone, the forests seem to rob the mind of a mendicant who isn’t immersed in samādhi. I get rid of that fear and dread just as it comes, while remaining just as I am
My energy was roused up and unflagging, my mindfulness was established and lucid, my body was tranquil and undisturbed, and my mind was immersed in samādhi 4 jhanas  and 3 knowledge
column16:
Those ascetics and brahmins summon unskillful fear and dread because of these defects in their conduct and livelihood; full of desire for sensual pleasures, with acute lust; full of ill will, with hateful intention; overcome with dullness and drowsines;  are restless, with no peace of mind; doubting and uncertain; who glorify themselves and put others down; are cowardly and craven; enjoy possessions, honor, and popularity; lazy and lack energy; in their mindfulness & unalert; lack immersion, with straying mind and are witless and stupid
If there’s anyone of whom it may be rightly said that a being not liable to delusion has arisen in the world for the welfare and happiness of the people, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans, it’s of me that this should be said

That’s why these things are mixed, not separate

The words of another and proper attention

column14:
The layman visākha asks the nun dhammadinnā about various difficult matters, including some of the highest meditation attainments. The Buddha  fully endorses her answers.
Dhammadinna the nun fields a series of Dhamma questions put to her by her former husband: questions on self-identification, cessation, penetration into the true nature of feeling, and the attainment of nibbana.
column15:
These five grasping aggregates are identity. 
That is: form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness
Breathing is a physical process. Placing the mind and keeping it connected are verbal processes. Perception and feeling are mental processes.
Verbal processes cease first, then physical, then mental
Anything felt physically or mentally as pleasant or enjoyable. This Is pleasant feeling. Anything Felt physically or mentally as painful or unpleasant. This Is painful feeling. Anything Felt physically or mentally as neither pleasurable nor painful. This Is neutral feeling
The underlying tendency for greed underlies pleasant feeling. The underlying tendency for repulsion underlies painful feeling. The underlying tendency for ignorance underlies neutral feeling
column16:
The origin of identity is the craving that leads to future rebirth, mixed up with relishing and greed, taking pleasure in various different realms. the fading away and cessation of that very same craving with nothing left over; giving it away, letting it go, releasing it, and not adhering to it is the cessation of identity
Unification of the mind is samadhi.  The four kinds of mindfulness meditation are the foundations of samadhi  the four right efforts are the prerequisites for samadhi . The Cultivation, development, and making much of these very same things is the development of samadhi
To attain the cessation of perception and feeling one does not think: ‘I will enter ’ or ‘I am entering or ‘I have entered the cessation of perception and feeling.’ Rather, their mind has been previously developed so as to lead to such a state
Pleasant feeling is pleasant when it remains and painful when it perishes. 
Painful feeling is painful when it remains and pleasant when it perishes.Neutral Feeling is pleasant when there is knowledge, and painful when there is ignorance
With first jhana one he abandons passion, nursing yearning for the unexcelled liberations, there arises within him sorrow based on that yearning. With that he abandons resistance, and with four jhana one  abandons ignorance

column14: The Buddha  explains how taking up different practices may have harmful or beneficial results. The memorable simile of the creeper shows how insidious temptations can be
column15:
Pleasant now with future pain: renunciantes throw themselves into sensual pleasures, after death, they’re reborn in a place of loss, for it is because of sensual pleasures that they will feel pain
Painful now but results in future pleasure:  when someone is ordinarily full of acute greed, hate, and delusion. They often feel the pain and sadness that greed, hate, and delusion bring. 
They lead the full and pure spiritual life in pain and sadness, weeping, when their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in a good place
column16:

column14:
The Buddha  ascends to a high heavenly realm where he engages in a cosmic contest with a powerful divinity, who had fallen into the delusion that he was eternal and all-powerful
The Buddha  disarms two powerful antagonists through his profound understanding of the nature of consciousness
column15:
Because what is actually impermanent, not lasting, transient, incomplete, and perishable, he says is permanent, everlasting, eternal, complete, and imperishable
You are Māra the wicked. And Brahmā, Brahmā’s assembly, and Brahmā’s retinue have all fallen into your hands; they’re under your sway
Consciousness that is invisible, infinite, radiant all round—*that’s* what is not within the scope of experience based on earth, water, fire, air, creatures, gods, the creator, Brahmā, the gods of streaming radiance, the gods replete with glory, the gods of abundant fruit, the overlord, and the all
Brahmā, his assembly, and his retinue, their minds full of wonder and amazement, thought,  we’ve never before seen or heard of any other ascetic or brahmin with psychic power and might like the ascetic gotama
column16:
Where there is being born, growing old, dying, passing away, and being reborn, he says that there’s no being born, growing old, dying, passing away, or being reborn
Brahmā, I understand your range and your light: a galaxy extends a thousand times as far
And there you wield your power.
You know the high and low, 
The passionate and dispassionate, 
And the coming and going of sentient beings 

Having directly known all as all, and having directly known that which does not fall within the scope of experience based on all, I did not identify with all, I did not identify regarding all, I did not identify as all, I did not identify ‘all is mine’, I did not enjoy all
Because the realized one has given up the defilements—corruptions that lead to future lives and are hurtful, resulting in suffering and future rebirth, old age, and death

The Buddha ’s chief disciples, Sāriputta and Moggallāna, use a simile of a tarnished bowl to illustrate the blemishes of the mind and conduct. They emphasize how the crucial thing is not so much whether there are blemishes, but whether we are aware of them

column15:
Blemish’ is a term for the spheres of bad, unskillful wishes and when their wishes are not fulfill anger and that bitterness are both blemishes.
Who doesn’t have a blemish and does understand it. You can expect that they won’t focus on the feature of beauty, and because of that, lust won’t infect their mind. 
Who doesn’t have a blemish and doesn't understand it won't make effort to guard his mind.
column16:
Person who has a blemish and does not understand it. You can expect that they won’t make an effort to give up that blemish. 
Person who has a blemish and does understand it will make an effort to get rid of them.
Gentlemen who went forth out of faith. They’re not devious, deceitful, and sneaky, restless, insolent, fickle, gossipy, and loose-tongued. They guard their sense doors and eat in moderation, and they are dedicated to wakefulness. They care about the ascetic life, and keenly respect the training. They’re not indulgent or slack, nor are they leaders in backsliding, neglecting seclusion. They’re energetic and determined. They’re mindful, with situational awareness, immersion, and unified minds; wise, not stupid.

column3: Ascetic Who Behaved Like a Dog
column14:
Some ascetics in ancient india undertook extreme practices, such as a vow to behave like an ox or a dog. The Buddha  meets two such individuals, and is reluctantly pressed to reveal the kammic outcomes of such practice
Act like a dog, and that's what you'll become. The moral: choose your actions with care.
column15:
This is how a being is born from a being. 
For what you do brings about your rebirth, and when you’re reborn contacts affect you.This Is why I say that sentient beings are heirs to their deeds. 
Someone who develops the dog observance fully and uninterruptedly. They develop a dog’s ethics, a dog’s mentality, and a dog’s behavior
When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in the company of dogs
column16:
There are dark deeds with dark results;
Bright deeds with bright results;dark and bright deeds with dark and bright results; andneither dark nor bright deeds with neither dark nor bright results, which lead to the ending of deeds.
But if they have such a view: ‘by this precept or observance or mortification or spiritual life, may I become one of the gods!’ This is their wrong view. 
An individual with wrong view is reborn in one of two places, I say: hell or the animal realm

column15: The Buddha  explains the criteria for determining whether or not something is worth saying. This discourse is a beautiful example of the Buddha 's skill as teacher: not only does he talk about right speech, but he also demonstrates right speech in action
column16: Realized one does not utter speech that he knows to be untrue, false, and harmful, and which is disliked by others. Neither He utter speech that he knows to be true and substantive, but which is harmful and disliked by others. The Realized one knows the right time to speak so as to explain what he knows to be true, substantive, and beneficial, but which is disliked by others. The Realized one does not utter speech that he knows to be untrue, false, and harmful, but which is liked by others. The Realized one does not utter speech that he knows to be true and substantive, but which is harmful, even if it is liked by others. The Realized one knows the right time to speak so as to explain what he knows to be true, substantive, and beneficial, and which is liked by others.
column17: A boy that put a stick or stone in his mouth and the father that take it out using a hooked finger of my right hand, even if it drew blood, like the Buddha that sometimes utter that is disliked by othera

column14:
The Buddha  resolves a disagreement on the number of kinds of feelings that he taught, pointing out that different ways of teaching are appropriate in different contexts, and should not be a cause of disputes. He goes on to show the importance of pleasure in developing higher meditation
The Buddha  discusses the range of possible pleasures and joys, and concludes by advocating a pleasure that goes beyond feeling. [the text of this sutta is almost identical to that of sn 36.19.]
column15:
I’ve explained the teaching in all these different ways. 
This being so, you can expect that those who do concede, approve, or agree with what has been well spoken will live in harmony, appreciating each other
 when the Buddha  describes what’s included in happiness, he’s not just referring to pleasant feeling. 
The realized one describes pleasure as included in happiness wherever it’s found, and in whatever context
column16:
In one explanation I’ve spoken of two feelings. In another explanation I’ve spoken of three feelings, or five, six, eighteen, thirty-six, or a hundred and eight feelings. 
There are five kinds of sensual pleasures, finer pleasures are the 4 jhanas, finer pleasures are the 4 immaterial jhanas and the finest is cessation of perceptions and feelings

The Buddha  teaches a group of uncommitted householders how to use a rational reflection to arrive at practices and principles that are guaranteed to have a good outcome, even if we don’t know all the variables
The Buddha  explains to a group of householders how to navigate skillfully through the maze of wrong views.
column15:
Those who don’t see that unskillful qualities are full of drawbacks, sordidness, and corruption, or that skillful qualities have the benefit and cleansing power of renunciation.
Wrong view gives rise to these many bad, unskillful qualities—wrong view, wrong thought, wrong speech, contradicting the noble ones, convincing others to accept untrue teachings, and glorifying oneself and putting others down.
 do a bad deed when they kill, steal, break into houses, plunder wealth, steal from isolated buildings, commit highway robbery, commit adultery, and lie, evil comes of that, and an outcome of evil
There actually is another world, action actually does have an effect, there are totally formless states
Without knowing or seeing, it would not be appropriate for me to take one side and declare, 
‘this is the only truth, other ideas are silly, but reflecting wisely, they simply practice for disillusionment, dispassion, and cessation regarding forms.
Mortifies themselves, committed to the practice of mortifying themselves.
One person mortifies others, committed to the practice of mortifying others.One Person mortifies themselves and others, committed to the practice of mortifying themselves and others.
They live without wishes in the present life, extinguished, cooled, experiencing bliss, having become holy in themselves
column16:
Who have this doctrine and view: 
‘there’s no meaning in giving, sacrifice, or offerings. There’s no fruit or result of good and bad deeds. There’s no afterlife. There’s no obligation to mother and father. No beings are reborn spontaneously. And there’s no ascetic or brahmin who is well attained and practiced, and who describes the afterlife after realizing it with their own insight.  undertake and implement bad conduct by way of body, speech, and mind.
That individual with wrong views is criticized by sensible people in the present life as being an immoral individual of wrong view and also  after death, they will be reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell
Giving and sacrificing and encouraging others to do the same, merit comes of that, and an outcome of merit. 
In giving, self-control, restraint, and truthfulness there is merit and outcome of merit.’
Sentient beings are corrupted with cause and reason. 
There is a cause and condition for the purification of sentient beings. Sentient Beings are purified with cause and reason. There Is power, energy, manly strength and vigor. It Is not the case that all sentient beings, all living creatures, all beings, all souls lack control, power, and energy, or that, molded by destiny, circumstance, and nature, they experience pleasure and pain in the six classes of rebirth
It is possible 
That I will be guaranteed rebirth among the gods who are formless and made of perception. Now, owing to form, bad things are seen: taking up the rod and the sword, quarrels, arguments, and fights, accusations, divisive speech, and lies. But Those things don’t exist where it is totally formless
One person doesn’t mortify either themselves or others, committed to the practice of not mortifying themselves or others.

column16:
Each of these ten convictions is the the trick of views, the fetter of views. They’re beset with anguish, distress, and fever. They don’t lead to disillusionment, dispassion, cessation, peace, insight, awakening, and extinguishment. Seeing This drawback I avoid all these convictions
Any form, feelings, perceptions, fabrications or consciousness by which a realized one might be described has been cut off at the root and unable to arise in the future. A Realized one is freed from reckoning in those terms. For this principle is deep, hard to see, hard to understand, peaceful, sublime, beyond the scope of reason, subtle, comprehensible to the astute.

column14:
Wanderer teaches that a person has reached the highest attainment when they keep four basic ethical precepts. The Buddha ’s standards are considerably higher.
The highest attainment is not simply the abandoning of unskillful actions and a reversion to childlike harmlessness. It requires first developing skillful habits and skillful resolves, and then letting them go.
column15:
Skillful deeds by way of body and speech, and purified livelihood, and they stem from a mind that is free from greed, hate, and delusion, their cessation is when a mendicant behaves ethically, but they don’t identify with their ethical behavior. And They truly understand the freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom
Someone is practicing for the cessation of unskillful behaviors and thoughts when generates enthusiasm, tries, makes an effort, exerts the mind, and strives so that bad, unskillful qualities don’t arise, and that bad, unskillful qualities that have arisen are given up
Thoughts of sensuality, of malice, and of cruelty are unskillful, they stem from perceptions of sensuality, malice, and cruelty and they cease without anything left over in first jhana
When an individual has these ten qualities, I describe them as an invincible ascetic—accomplished in the skillful, excelling in the skillful, attained to the highest attainment
column16:
Unskillful deeds by way of body and speech, and bad livelihood, they stem from a mind that has greed, hate, and delusion, their cessation it’s when a mendicant gives up bad conduct by way of body, speech, and mind, and develops good conduct by way of body, speech, and mind; they give up wrong livelihood and earn a living by right livelihood,
Someone practicing for the cessation of skillful behaviors and thoughts, they generate enthusiasm, try, make an effort, exert the mind, and strive so that skillful qualities arise, and  that skillful qualities that have arisen remain, are not lost, but increase, mature, and are completed by development
Thoughts of renunciation, good will, and harmlessness are called skillful, they stem from  perceptions of renunciation, good will, and harmlessness, and they cease without anything left over in the second jhana
Someone who has an adept’s right view, right thought, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right immersion, right knowledge, and right freedom
column17: A person who do no bad deeds with their body; speak no bad words; think no bad thoughts; and don’t earn a living by bad livelihood, has attained the same level as a baby

The Buddha  gives a detailed explanation of how true understanding gradually emerges through spiritual education

column15:
This is the extent of master gotama’s praise that I have learned. But his praises are not confined to this,for the praise of master gotama is limitless
These five things can be seen to turn out in two different ways. For a sensible person who is preserving truth this is not sufficient to come to the definite conclusion: 
‘this is the only truth, other ideas are silly
Approaches and scrutinizes them for three kinds of things: 
Things that arouse greed, things that provoke hate, and things that promote delusion. ‘Does this venerable have any qualities that arouse any of these
That’s how the awakening to truth is defined, and by the cultivation, development, and making much of these very same things there is the arrival at the truth
column16:
He went forth from an eminent, rich, affluent, and wealthy  family of unbroken aristocratic lineage while he was still young; he is ethical,  a good speaker, teacher of teachers, he has ended sensual desire, teaches the efficacy of deeds and action, many thousands of deities, brahmins and kings  have gone for refuge for life to him, he has this good reputation: ‘that blessed one is perfected, a fully awakened Buddha , accomplished in knowledge and conduct, holy, knower of the world, supreme guide for those who wish to train, teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed, he has the thirty-two marks of a great man
Faith, preference, oral tradition, reasoned contemplation, and acceptance of a view after consideration,  preserve truth by saying, ‘such is the view I have accepted after any of this 5 things, but they don’t yet come to the definite conclusion: 
‘this is the only truth, other ideas are silly.
Scrutinizing them they find: 
‘this venerable has no such qualities that arouse greed.Rather, that venerable has bodily and verbal behavior like that of someone without greed. And The principle that they teach is deep, hard to see, hard to understand, peaceful, sublime, beyond the scope of reason, subtle, comprehensible to the astute. It’s Not easy for someone with greed to teach this.
After scrutinizing they place faith in them. When faith has arisen they approach the teacher. They pay homage, lend an ear, hear the teachings, remember the teachings, reflect on their meaning, and accept them after consideration. Then enthusiasm springs up; they make an effort, weigh up, and persevere. Persevering, they directly realize the ultimate truth, and see it with penetrating wisdom

column14: A corrupt tax-collector is redeemed by his encounter with venerable Sāriputta
column15:
Someone who behaves in a principled and just manner for the sake of their family.
For principled and moral conduct is better than unprincipled and immoral conduct
Mendicants, Sāriputta, after establishing dhanañjāni in the inferior Brahmā realm, got up from his seat and left while there was still more left to do.”
column16:
Someone was to behave in an unprincipled and unjust way for the sake of their family.Because Of this the wardens of hell would drag them to hell. 
Could they get out of being dragged to hell by pleading that they had acted for the sake of their parents? Or could their parents save them by pleading that the acts had been done for their sake?
Path to companionship with Brahmā
Firstly, a person meditates spreading a heart full of love, compassion, rejoice or equanimity  to one direction, and to the second, and to the third, and to the fourth. In the same way above, below, across, everywhere, all around, they spread a heart full of love, compassion, rejoice or equanimity to the whole world—abundant, expansive, limitless, free of enmity and ill will

column14: Two brahmin students ask the Buddha  about what makes a brahmin: birth or deeds? The Buddha  points out that, while the species of animals are determined by birth, for humans what matters is how you chose to live. This discourse anticipates the modern view that there are no such things as clearly defined racial differences among humans
column15:
They have nothing before or after, 
Or even in between; 
One with nothing, by not grasping: 
That’s who I call a brahmin
You’re a brahmin by your deeds you’re a farmer by your deeds, 
By deeds you’re a professional; 
You’re a trader by your deeds, 
By deeds are you an employee you’re a bandit by your deeds, 
By deeds you’re a soldier; 
You’re a sacrificer by your deeds, 
By deeds you’re a ruler
column16:
They’ve given up human bonds, 
And gone beyond heavenly bonds; 
Detached from all attachments: 
That’s who I call a brahmin
In this way in accord with truth, 
The astute regard deeds. 
Seeing dependent origination, 
They’re expert in deeds and their results
