column15:
Here he is happy, after death he is happy,
the meritorious one is happy in both places,
he is happy...
seeing the purity of his own deeds.
column16:
“He abused me, he struck at me, 
he overcame me, he robbed me,”
those who bear these ill-will,
their hatred is never appeased.

column14:
The fragrance of flowers goes not against the wind,
nor does sandalwood or pinwheel or saffron,
but the fragrance of the good goes against the wind,
the true person’s fragrance permeates all directions.
column15:
Just like a beautiful flower, 
which has colour, and has fragrance,
so are well-spoken words fruitful 
for the one who does act on them.
column16:
The End-Maker takes control of 
the one whose mind is attached to collecting flowers,
though he is unfulfilled with sense pleasures.

column14:
Not through a rain of coins is satisfaction found for sense desires,
the wise one knowing: 
“Sense pleasures have little joy, much suffering,”
does not find delight even in heavenly pleasures.
The disciple of the Perfect Sambuddha delights in craving’s destruction.
column15:
That one who is overcome by these low cravings in the world, 
which are difficult to get past,
for him griefs increase 
like grass that has been rained upon.
column16:
Be free of the past, be free of the future,
be free of the present, after crossing over all existence,
with mind liberated in every way,
you will not return to birth and old age.

column14:
Easily done are things not good, 
and unbeneficial for oneself,
but only those beneficial and good 
are done by the wise.
column15:
The sage gradually, 
little by little, moment by moment,
should remove the stain from himself, 
like a smith removes the stain from silver.
column16:
Knowing the essential in what is essential, 
and the unessential in what is unessential,
they understand what is essential, 
and resort to right intention.

column14:
Stupid fools live having themselves as their own foes,
committing wicked deeds, 
which produce bitter fruit.
column15:
The fool thinks there is success, 
when he speaks words that are rough,
but for the one who knows, 
endurance is the success of the good.
column16:
The fool who conceives he is a fool, 
is at least wise in that matter,
the fool who is proud of his wisdom, 
he is said to be a fool indeed.

column14:
That man who wraps up rotting fish with the best fragrant grass,
makes the fragrant grass smell rotten, 
and so with those who associate with fools.
column15:
If one who does no wickedness associates with those who do,
he is suspected of wickedness, 
and his disrepute increases.
column16:
Even if a fool attends on a wise man for his whole life long,
he does not learn Dhamma, 
like the spoon learns not the taste of curry.

column14:
Like a cowherd with a stick drives cattle to pasture,
so do old age and death overpower living beings.
column15:
Everyone trembles at sticks, 
for all of them life is dear,
comparing oneself with others, 
one should not hurt or have them hurt.
column16:
One should regard someone who shows your faults 
just like one who points out hidden treasure,
one should keep company with 
such a sagacious person who reproves you;
keeping company with such is surely better for you, not worse.

column14:
The one who finds pleasure in the Dhamma, 
delights in Dhamma, reflects on Dhamma,
the monastic who remembers Dhamma, 
does not abandon the Dhamma.
column15:
The Dhamma protects the one who lives by the Dhamma,
the Dhamma well-practised is set on happiness,{61}
this is the advantage of the Dhamma well-practised,
he who lives by the Dhamma does not go to a bad destination.
column16:
Whoever has gone for refuge to the Buddha, 
the Dhamma and the Saṅgha,
and who sees as it really is the four noble truths.
That is a secure refuge,

column14:
If, for even one living being, one with an uncorrupt mind,
has loving-kindness, there is wholesomeness in that,
but the one with compassion in mind for all living beings,
 that noble one makes abundant merit.
column15:
Then he who with a mind of loving-kindness 
has compassion for all living beings,
having loving-kindness towards all beings, 
he has no one who is hated.
column16:
He who neither kills, nor has killed, 
conquers, nor has conquered,
having loving-kindness towards all beings, 
he has no one who is hated.

column14:
in solitude, where it is hard to delight,
one should seek to delight in that place, 
having given up sense pleasures, and having no possessions,
he should purify the self of defilements of mind in every way.
column15:
for those who always properly undertake 
mindfulness of the body
who do not practice what is not to be done, 
persisting in what is to be done,
for those mindful ones, those fully aware, 
their pollutants are destroyed.
column16:
For those devoted to being alert, 
who train both by day and by night,
who are intent on Nibbāna, 
the pollutants are laid to rest.

column14:
The wise are restrained bodily, 
verbally and also mentally,
the wise are restrained in every way, 
they are indeed very well-restrained.
column15:
Even though reciting abundant scriptures,
the heedless fellow, who does not do what they say,
like a cowboy counting other’s cattle,
does not partake of the ascetic life.
column16:
One should speak out the truth, one should not get angry, 
when requested you should give, if only a little,
through these three conditions 
one can go to the presence of the gods.

column14:
If you should find a prudent, wise companion, 
one who lives well, a wise one,
overcoming all your troubles
you should live with that one, glad and mindful.
column15:
If you do not find a prudent, wise companion, 
one who lives well, a wise one,
like a king who abandons his conquered kingdom,
one should live alone like a solitary elephant in the forest.
column16:
It is better to live alone, 
there can be no companionship with a fool,
one should live alone and not do anything bad,
unconcerned like a solitary elephant in the forest.

column14:
Not the wrongs of others, 
or what others have done or have not done one should consider, 
but what has been done and not done by oneself.
column15:
If one regards oneself as dear one should guard oneself right well,
for happiness is not easy to gain by those who do wrong.
column16:
Whoever reviles the worthy teaching 
of the Noble Ones who live by Dhamma,
that stupid one, depending on wicked views,
makes himself the same as his enemy wishes him to be.

column14:
Having faith, virtue and energy,
concentration and insight into the Dhamma,
well-established in patience, meekness and concentration,
they have come to the essence of wisdom and learning.
column15:
Faith is a person’s travelling companion,
he would not accept travelling without faith,
from that there will be fame and renown for him,
and when he abandons the body he goes to heaven.
column16:
He who has removed impetuosity, 
displeasure from his mind,
with confident mind, happy, 
he can understand well-spoken words.

column14:
Like a fish thrown up on dry land, 
pulled out from its watery home,
the mind is agitated, 
one ought to throw off the sway of Māra.
column15:
For the mind that is difficult to subdue, flighty, 
flitting wherever it will,
restraint is good, 
a restrained mind brings happiness.
column16:
Just as rain does not penetrate a house with thatching that is good,
so passion, hatred and delusion cannot penetrate a mind that is well-developed.

column14:
The eightfold is the best of paths, 
four principles the best of truths,
dispassion the best of states, 
the Visionary the best of men.
column15:
For as long as an atom of desire
of a man for his kin is not cut down,
the mind is in bondage there,
like a calf in bondage to mother’s milk.
column16:
All conditions are impermanent, 
All components of mind and body are without self,
when one sees this with wisdom,
then one grows tired of suffering – 
this is the path to purity.

column14:
Whatever the alms or the sacrifice in the world
the one seeking merit may give for a year,
all that comes not to a quarter of the merit –
better is the worship of the upright.
column15:
One might give alms impartially with a thousand coins of money 
month by month for a hundred years;
 but that is not worth a sixteenth part 
of having confidence in the Buddha, Dhamma and Sangha
column16:
One might live for a hundred years, 
unestablished in the True Dhamma,
 but a life of one day is better, 
for one who knows the True Dhamma.

column14:
That one who removes the passion, hatred, delusion, anger, conceit that has arisen,
as he would remove pervasive snake venom with medicines,
that monk abandons the near and far shore,
like a snake who has abandoned its old, worn-out skin.
column15:
That one who cuts off craving without remainder,
having dried up that quick-flowing stream,
that monk abandons the near and far shore,
like a snake who has abandoned its old, worn-out skin
column16:
For the one with no distress that has arisen,
having uprooted all unwholesome roots,
that monk abandons the near and far shore,
like a snake who has abandoned its old, worn-out skin.
column17: snake snake who has abandoned its old, worn-out skin, like Awakened Ones

column14:
The foolish and stupid people cultivate heedlessness,
but the sagacious one guards heedfulness 
just as his greatest wealth.
column15:
Whoever before was heedless, 
but later is not heedless,
he, being mindful, 
can overcome clinging to the world.
column16:
One should not follow lowly things, 
one should not abide heedlessly,
one should not follow a wrong view, 
one should not foster worldliness.

column14:
Not because of matted hair, 
family or birth is one a true brahmin,
he who wards off wickedness, 
 in every way, 
he is called a brahmin.
column15:
Like water on the lotus leaf, 
like a mustard seed on a needle,
he who is unsmeared by desires, 
that one I say is a brahmin.
column16:
The deeply wise sagacious one, 
skilled in what is path and not path,
who has reached the ultimate good, 
that one I say is a brahmin.

column14:
That monastic who dwells in loving-kindness, 
with faith in Buddha’s dispensation,
has penetrated the state of peace, 
the joy in stilling of all conditions,
here and now there is Nibbāna, 
the unsurpassed release from all bonds.
column15:
With uplifted mind, happy, 
having overcome what is dear and not dear,
then with lots of happiness, 
the monastic should wander mindfully.
column16:
Calm in body and calm in mind, 
having calmness and composure,
having thrown off worldly gain 
the monastic is called one at peace.

column14:
Friends are good whenever need arises,
at the break-up of life merit is good,
being content with everything is good,
the abandoning of all wickedness is good.
column15:
Meeting with the noble is pleasant, 
living with good people is pleasant,
through not meeting foolish people 
one will constantly be happy.
column16:
Therefore do not hold anything as loved, 
for speaking of the loved is loathsome.
There are no knots for those 
who hold nothing as loved or as unloved.

column14:
If, by renouncing a small good, 
he might see a good that is large,
the wise one should renounce that small good, 
seeing the good that is extensive.
column15:
There are surely true people everywhere,
the good do not talk of desiring sense-pleasures;
when touched by pleasure or by suffering,
true people are not elated or depressed.
column16:
The victor generates hatred, 
the defeated one finds suffering,
the one at peace lives happily, 
having abandoned victory and defeat.

column14:
Whatever griefs or lamentations there are,
and the many kinds of suffering in the world,
these all arise because of love,
without loves, these do not originate.
column15:
Therefore they are happy and free from grief,
who are without love for anything in the world,
therefore those wanting what is griefless, dust-free,
should not have love for anything in the world.
column16:
The one who, steady in virtue, 
throws out any impurity,
endowed with restraint and truth, 
is indeed worthy of the renunciant’s robe.

column14:
A wicked deed that has been done, 
like milk, does not turn all at once,
smouldering, it follows the fool, 
like a fire covered with ashes.
column15:
He who offends against the inoffensive one,
a purified and passionless person:
that wicked deed then returns to the fool,
like fine dust that is thrown against the wind.
column16:
Like a merchant on a fearful path, 
with few friends and great wealth,
as one loving life would avoid poison, 
so should one avoid wicked deeds.

column15:
Action, knowledge, righteousness,
Virtue, an excellent life:
By this are mortals purified,
Not by clan or wealth.
column16:
Where name-and-form ceases,
Stops without remainder:
By understanding that Dhamma here
They cut through the bondage of existence.

column14: The Buddha  is asked about the future destiny of people who are stingy and those who are generous.
column15:
Those who are stingy here in the world,
Niggardly folk, revilers,
People who create obstacles
For others engaged in giving alms:
They might be reborn in bad place
column16:
Those here who, on gaining the human state,
Are amiable and generous,
Confident in the Buddha  and the dhamma
And deeply respectful towards the saṅgha,
These brighten up the heavens

column14: A brahmin farmer criticizes the Buddha  for failing to produce food, merely living off the work of others. But the Buddha  shows that his true work is spiritual
column15:
Faith is the seed, austerity the rain,
Wisdom my yoke and plough;
Shame is the pole, mind the yoke-tie,
Mindfulness my ploughshare and goad
column16:
Energy is my beast of burden,
Carrying me to security from bondage.
It goes ahead without stopping
To where, having gone, one does not sorrow

And wisdom is what instructs him.

column15:

Misery to one filled with delight.

That’s how you should know me, friend

column16: “associate only with the virtuous! Try to get close to the virtuous! Understanding the true teaching of the good, You’re released from all suffering.”

column14: The deity khema utters a series of verses in praise of good deeds. The Buddha  responds with a simile for someone who departs the path of the good
column15: It’s not good to do a deed After which you will regret. You experience the result Weeping, with a tearful face
column16: So too, an idiot departs the good To follow what’s against the good. Fallen in the jaws of death, They fret like their axle’s broken.

column14: Some monks in kosala fell into negligence, and were admonished by the deity jantu
column15:

column15:

By means of travelling [through the world],
Yet without reaching the world’s end
There is no release from suffering
column16: It is in this fathom-high carcass endowed with perception and mind that I make known the world, the origin of the world, the cessation of the world, and the way leading to the cessation of the world.

column15:

Unsmeared with regard

habits or practices, merit or evil,
not creating anything here,
he’s let go

seizing it there

At death a person abandons
what he supposes as mine.

shouldn’t incline
to be devoted to mine-ness.

Everywhere, the sage
independent

but then resorts
to sexual intercourse

is called vile in the world,
a person run-of-the-mill.

not pitting view against view—
who have nothing here grasped as supreme?

for sensual pleasures,
should be limpid in mind.
Skilled in all mental qualities,
he, the monk, should wander
mindfully.

He who in the midst of sensualities,
follows the holy life,

the monk who is

unbound:

column15:
They hoped for, liked, longed for, so they sacrificed—
they longed for sensuality,
dependent on gain.
Those who take on the yoke
of sacrifice,
impassioned with
the passion for becoming,
have not crossed over birth &aging.

He who has fathomed
the high &low in the world,
for whom there is nothing
perturbing in the world—
evaporated, undesiring,
untroubled, at peace—

column15:
You ask me the source of stress.
From acquisition as cause
the many forms of stress
come into being in the world.

Therefore, discerning,
you shouldn’t create acquisitions
as you stay focused on
the birth &origin of stress.

No one in the world, Dhotaka,
can I release from perplexity.
But knowing the most excellent Dhamma,
you will cross over this flood.
column16:
Whatever you’re alert to,
above, below,
across, in between:
Knowing it as a bond in the world,
don’t create craving
for becoming or non-.

Mindfully focused on nothingness,
relying on ‘There isn’t,’
you should cross over the flood.
Abandoning sensuality,
abstaining from conversations,
keep watch for the ending of
craving, night &day.
column16:
As a flame overthrown by the force of the wind
goes to an end
that cannot be classified,2
so the sage freed from the name-body3
goes to an end
that cannot be classified.

like the moon on the fifteenth day.

now there’ll be no more future lives

such a monk sleeps at ease,

from the lay life to homelessness—
the ending of all fetters.

meditating tirelessly,

column15:

limitless and well-developed;
gradually consolidated
as it was taught by the Buddha.
column16:

who is always seeking purity,

column15:

column15:

this is the best happiness.

diligent

column15:

clear and unclouded,
of good morals, intelligent:
one would make an end of suffering
